newsitem.title: JAPAN: Excessive yen rise, fall undesirable -- Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Excessive yen rise, fall undesirable -- Sakakibara.

text.p: Senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said on Wednesday that neither an excessive rise nor fall of the yen is desirable.
He told Reuters that he does not have anything to say on currency moves beyond what Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told parliament earlier on Wednesday.
"What we can say now is that neither an excessive rise nor an excessive fall of the yen is desirable," Sakakibara said.
Asked if he is happy to see the dollar recovering to a level above 114 yen, Sakakibara said he would like to decline to comment on that question.
Earlier on Wednesday Mitsuzuka said worries over the excessive weakening of the yen had completely disappeared and that it was important for foreign exchange rates to stabilise.
He also said that Japan would deal "in a timely and appropriate way" with foreign exchange volatility and excessive movements.
